items.title: 68426_Nellie Lutcher oral history interview
items.q: Garland, her name was Mrs. Garland, lived below me

ctx.x: straight down Central Avenue. And as I got close to home, I just began to feel so terrible, and I said oh, my God, I hope I can make it home. So I got off the streetcar at my corner, you know, and walked on home, and I just barely made it. I was so happy to get home. And we lived upstairs in an apartment, and I went on upstairs and the first thing I did was sit on the side of the bed, and then I would lie down a little while, and then I'd sit up a little while, I'd lie down. Then I said well, I guess I'd better…

So there was an old lady who lived below me. Garland, her name was Mrs. Garland, lived below me, and it so happened that she was home that day. She worked also. And she was home, and I looked out the window, out my back bedroom window, and I saw her in the yard, and so I called her and told her. I asked her if she would come upstairs a little while, so she says, "Oh, yes, I'll be up in a minute." So she took her time and she finally came upstairs. And I told her, I said, "Look, I'm not feeling good. You know, I…
down and I'd sit up and I'd lie down and I'd sit up and I'd go to the bathroom. Oh, I carried on, you know, never thinking that this was so close to happening.
